seoTitle: Hreflang Code Checker: Valid ISO Language and Region Codes
metaDescription: Check hreflang values against ISO 639-1, ISO 3166-1 and ISO 15924 lists. Catches en-UK, jp, es-419 and underscores, with the corrected form.
intro: Checks each hreflang value against the official language, region and script code lists and tells you the correct form, for example en-GB instead of en-UK.
why:
Google ignores hreflang values it cannot read, and the common mistakes are all about codes: UK instead of GB, jp instead of ja, a country code on its own, an underscore, a three-letter language, or the numeric region 419. The format check in other tools accepts many of these. This one checks membership in the ISO 639-1 language list, the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region list and the ISO 15924 script list.

Rules follow the Google page on localized versions, read 2026-10-23. The check says nothing about whether people in a region really read that language.
howTo: Paste codes one per line, or whole link tags or code | URL lines.
Read the verdict for each code.
Apply the suggested form where one is given.
Run again until all are OK.

faq.a: It is a UN M.49 region. Google names it as unsupported; use es or a country such as es-MX.
Google reads codes case-insensitively. The tool suggests the usual form, de-AT, as a review note.

faq.q: Why is eu listed as OK?
faq.a: eu is Basque. The tool warns about this in confusable cases such as be, se and ca when used alone.
ISO 639-1, ISO 3166-1 and ISO 15924 from the Debian iso-codes package.
